output.summary: KEP-5313 proposes a vendor-neutral, namespaced, data-only PlacementDecision API that standardizes the "which clusters" output of multicluster schedulers, so consumers (GitOps engines, orchestrators, rollout controllers, AI/ML pipelines) can read one format from any scheduler. Its status is provisional at alpha stage, since 2025-11-25.
output.rationale: Each multicluster scheduler publishes its own placement-decision API, so every consumer needs custom integration code per scheduler, which the KEP calls an integration explosion. The KEP scopes the standard to the decision output only: it leaves placement requests and workload deployment vendor-specific, and it requires each cluster reference to map to a ClusterProfile. The status is provisional, and the sources do not describe any review outcome or acceptance beyond that.

alternatives.option: Status quo: each scheduler ships its own placement API
alternatives.why_not: The KEP says this leads to consumer bloat and vendor lock-in, with each consumer writing separate code for every scheduler.

alternatives.option: Extend the Work API to carry scheduling details
alternatives.why_not: The KEP says this overloads a workload syncing API with scheduling details, coupling the where with the what.

evidence.quote: This KEP introduces a vendor neutral `PlacementDecision` API that standardizes the output of multicluster placement calculations.
Example: 10 consumers with 10 schedulers needs 100 separate integrations today, but only 20 integrations with this API
What this API standardizes: The "which clusters" answer (the decision output).
Extending `Work API`: overloads a workload syncner API with scheduling details which couples the where with the what.
